title: phase_membrane under a PhySim-style apparatus: its division survives dynamics noise of sd 0.01 per step when the concentrations get noise proportional to their value (and the phase field additive noise), and two probe arrays like PhySim's tell the world from its deciding ablations by an energy-score ratio of 1.8-5.5x within 100 t and 7-16x within 1000 t
summary:
Eval-readiness pilot. Question: does a collective world keep its behaviour under the things a PhySim evaluation needs (dynamics noise so that realizations differ, an apparatus of probe arrays), and can that apparatus see its mechanism? World: lab-1 phase_membrane (holder of reproduction-beyond-diffusion), unchanged, 128^2, dt 1, run to t=8000 as in its packs. Noise is added by a wrapper (files/pm_noise.py) before every step.

**Noise dose-response (labkit packs, seeds 0-2; persistent splits per seed, max generation).** files/noise_table.json and files/facts/.
- Baseline (same code path, sd 0): 9/7/9 persistent splits, generation 2-3.
- Additive on the phase field, proportional (sd x value) on S, K and L: sd 0.01 gives 8/10/8, generation 2-3 (files/sheet_proportional_0.01_s0.png looks like the baseline sheet: cells grow, pinch and divide to t=8000). sd 0.03: 0/2/0; sd 0.1: extinct.
- Additive on the phase field only: sd 0.01 gives 8/12/7, generation 1-3; sd 0.03: 3/16/0 (one seed extinct); sd 0.1: extinct.
- Plain additive on all four fields: see 20261028T1331-c00-evalready-pm-breakers (it tolerates 0.003 and dies at 0.01).

**Detectability (files/apparatus.py detect).** One prepared state (seed 0, t=4000, 17 bodies, median area 168 px; files/prep_s0.json). Two probe arrays shaped like PhySim's devices, a 13-node square lattice at spacing 6 px centred on a median body and a 19-node hex lattice at spacing 12 px on the largest other body, plus each field's mean and variance; readouts every 25 t; no injections. Eight members per arm with plain additive noise of sd 0.003 (a level the behaviour survives). The native ensemble forecasts a second native ensemble (different noise seeds) and each ablated ensemble branched from the same state; features standardized by the native ensemble's std. Energy score of the native forecast, at 100 / 300 / 1000 t (files/detect_s0_n0.003_w1000.json):
- native truth: 5.8 / 10.7 / 22.8
- link drift onto the wall off (chi=0): 10.6 / 53.8 / 164.0, ratio 1.8 / 5.0 / 7.2
- uniform mobility (gate=0, gateK=0; the diffusion-only twin): 31.9 / 101.6 / 358.7, ratio 5.5 / 9.5 / 15.7
- membrane tilt halved (a=2): 11.6 / 41.6 / 208.9, ratio 2.0 / 3.9 / 9.2
Without noise every member is identical (native energy score 0), so a deterministic world gives the score nothing to calibrate against.
limits:
- One world. The detectability test uses one seed, one prepared state and one probe placement (on bodies; PhySim's agent can move and dilate its devices). The pulse-free readout is the easiest case for the apparatus.
- The ablations start from the native prepared state and diverge over the window, so the ratios measure how fast each mechanism change shows in the probes, not how well a trained predictor would do.
- Energy scores use features standardized by the native ensemble's std, not PhySim's score groups; only ratios are meaningful.
- The noise forms are my choice. 'Proportional' noise on concentrations is one physical choice; demographic (sqrt) noise was not tried.
- Persistent splits come from labkit packs, which segment the summed matter field; I looked at the baseline and sd 0.01 sheets only.
- Lab-1 FACTS for this world report 12/10/9 persistent splits; the current labkit gives 9/7/9 on the same seeds with no noise, so compare within this table only.

finding.operator: robustness of division to dynamics noise of several forms, and visibility of the deciding mechanisms to PhySim-style probe arrays
finding.control: labkit packs on seeds 0-2 at sd 0, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1 for two noise forms (additive on phi only; additive on phi + proportional on S, K, L); 8-member ensembles from a t=4000 state under sd 0.003, native vs chi=0, gate=0 and a=2, probe arrays of 13 and 19 nodes plus global mean/variance
finding.result: division survives sd 0.01 in both forms (persistent splits 8/10/8 and 8/12/7 against 9/7/9) and fails at 0.03-0.1; energy-score ratio of the native forecast against ablated vs native truth 1.8-5.5x at 100 t, 3.9-9.5x at 300 t, 7.2-15.7x at 1000 t

implications: For PhySim evaluations of collective worlds: (1) a world needs a declared noise form suited to its fields, not one global additive noise (the companion negative shows the plain form kills this world at the same sd); (2) with such noise the world keeps its behaviour and member spread is nonzero, so the energy score has something to calibrate against; (3) plain probe readouts already separate the deciding ablations within a few hundred time units, and the separation grows with the window, so longer windows help. Next: the same battery on c53's fed vortices and c34's Marangoni rods (running), then a world contract (declared noise form, port maps, amplitude ranges, steps per tick) in the PhySim environment.
notes: Operator (c00) experiment for the PhySim eval-readiness line. Packs and frames were regenerated from files/pm_noise.py; frames.npz are not committed.
